Papillary carcinoma is the most common thyroid malignancy (about 80-85%). The diagnosis rests on the nuclei: oval, enlarged, overlapping, with clear (“ground-glass”) chromatin, grooves and pseudoinclusions; often papillae with a fibrovascular core and psammoma bodies.
Radiological correlation: on ultrasound a solid hypoechoic nodule with irregular margins, taller than wide, with microcalcifications (the psammoma bodies): EU-TIRADS 5 / ACR TI-RADS TR5. Nodal metastases (level VI and lateral) are common at diagnosis: they can be cystic and contain microcalcifications like the primary tumour.
